checks.note: AlertRuleAdminResource.update does findById → deleteById → save with no @Transactional, and the jakarta.persistence imports confirm Spring Data JPA 3.x where deleteById silently no-ops on a missing row — so concurrent PUTs both insert fresh rows with new generated ids (builder never sets id), and a retry on the old id hits the orElseThrow EntityNotFoundException despite the update having succeeded.

deleteUserInTransaction shows exactly the described pattern — unlocked findOneByLogin, !isActivated check, unconditional userRepository.delete(user), and its own javadoc admits the TOCTOU window is narrowed, not closed — but the finding's verification caveat (delete emits plain DELETE WHERE id=? and User has no @Version) depends on User.java and UserRepository.java, which are not shown; a @Version field would make the DELETE version-conditional and block deletion of a concurrently activated row.

matches.note: No reported finding mentions ROLE_LTD_ADMIN, HAS_ADMIN_ROLE, or any admin-tier authorization issue.

R1 covers the non-transactional delete-then-save with unvalidated body losing the rule and silencing alerting; R2 covers the remaining fragment that each successful PUT replaces the resource id.
